source.title: Shinners & Mahler's Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas
source.authors: Diggs, G. M. Jr.; Lipscomb, B. L.; O'Kennon, R. J.

morphology_documented.habit: Hickory tree (genus); no species height stated
morphology_documented.leaves: (7–)9–17 leaflets in key, falcate lateral leaflets usually asymmetric, glabrous below; leaflet teeth less conspicuous than pecan
morphology_documented.buds: Usually dark reddish brown; paired valvate bud scales (Carya key subgroup)
morphology_documented.bark: Exfoliating in long strips or plate-like scales (key)
morphology_documented.flowers: Male catkins on stalks (species contrast in key)
morphology_documented.fruit: Husk winged to base and splits vertically; subglobose to obovoid fruit up to 40 mm, somewhat laterally flattened, nuts as wide as long, wrinkled or furrowed, bitter kernel, fruits often grouped 3–4

source_scope_note: Historical species treatments and explicitly identified genus/key characteristics only; missing morphology not inferred.
unresolved_taxonomy_or_source_notes: Key characters distinguish water hickory from pecan, especially catkin stalk, nut compression, tooth prominence and fruit shape
Flora records mainly eastern counties, no BONAP Hays confirmation
preservation: Additive record only, original species and photo/credits/gallery unchanged
